messages:
incident-bot: Automatic page: SEV2 - geo-dns resolver anomalies detected impacting eu-west API endpoints. Paging @Aaron (SRE) and @Sara (NetOps). Please acknowledge and begin triage.

Aaron (SRE): acknowledged. Seeing surge in 502/504s from eu-west edge gateways. Error traces show upstream connection timeouts to cluster backends. Kicking off network checks.

Sara (NetOps): Correlating with external monitors: Cloudflare EU POPs show resolver timeouts and elevated latency. Route53 health-checks for eu records also show intermittent failures but with different timings. Adding logs.

John (Support): Customer reports: "Our app sees intermittent timeouts when calling your API from EU, started ~13:10 UTC." Affected: some PLG test orgs + 2 revenue customers in EU. No data corruption reported.

Aaron (SRE): Quick verification: run dig against our DNS from multiple public resolvers.

Aaron (SRE):
```
$ dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.com A +short
3.120.45.12
$ dig @ns1.redwooddns.net api.redwood.com +short
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

Maya (EngOps): We rolled a geo routing config ~25m ago to rebalance across CF and Route53 (change id chg-20260405-geo). Possible correlation. Pulling change history now.

Sara (NetOps): Cloudflare support acknowledges anomalies in eu-west resolvers (internal case CF-789). They see increased SERVFAIL rates for delegated NS queries from certain ISP resolvers. Route53 seems healthy but clients are still getting mixed answers due to resolver caching/proxying. Recommend temporarily flipping primary answer to Route53 and lowering TTL to speed client convergence.

Aaron (SRE): Proposed mitigation steps: 1) Update geo record to prefer Route53 (roll back the recent weight change), 2) Set TTL to 30s, 3) Pause CF-side traffic steering, 4) Monitor error rate and do canary for re-enable. Executing step 1 now.

Maya (EngOps): Applying change with CLI:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch file://emergency-route53-primary.json
```
Applied JSON (upsert to prefer route53):
```json
{"Comment":"emergency route53 primary","Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.com.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"route53-pri","Weight":100,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.120.45.12"}]}}]}
```

deploy-bot: route53 change C-0a1b2c3d accepted -> INSYNC.

Aaron (SRE): TTL lowered to 30s. Also temporarily disabled Cloudflare origin weighting so resolvers will prefer Route53 answers during mitigation.

Sara (NetOps): Opened CF support ticket (CF-789) and added our packet captures. Also created temporary CF page rule to avoid serving as primary until they confirm.

John (Support): Sending brief customer update: "We are routing EU traffic to an alternate DNS provider to mitigate resolver issues. TTL lowered to accelerate recovery. No data loss. Will update in 30 minutes." Will loop in AMs for impacted accounts.

Aaron (SRE): Observability: error-rate dropped from ~20% to ~3% within ~1 minute of change for EU gateways. Some ASNs still show elevated latency due to cached answers. Continuing to monitor.

Maya (EngOps): Confirming with dig from several locations:
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.com A +short
3.120.45.12
$ dig @9.9.9.9 api.redwood.com A +short
3.120.45.12
```

Sara (NetOps): Route53 health-check noise reduced. CF replied: "We're investigating resolver anomalies in eu-west POPs; keep TTL low while we work on mitigation." CF ticket updated CF-789.

Aaron (SRE): Plan to run a 10% Cloudflare canary once stable for 15 minutes. If errors remain <2% we can gradually increase. If >5% within 2m, revert to Route53 primary.

deploy-bot: canary policy applied: canary-id canary-20260405 -> 10% CF primary for eu queries.

John (Support): Updated status page: "Partial outage affecting EU traffic. Mitigation in progress; traffic rerouted to alternate DNS provider. Will follow up with timelines."

Raj (CTO): Good work. Please prepare a short incident brief and a list of customers who may need proactive outreach. Also check Dedicated customers that are EU-only.

Aaron (SRE): Handoff: I'll be off pager for next shift. Handing monitoring to Maya (EngOps) for 2h. Recorded runbook notes and actions in incident doc.

Maya (EngOps): ack. Current state: Route53 primary, TTL=30s, CF canary 10% healthy. Observability dashboards linked in incident doc. Packet captures saved to /var/incidents/geo-eu-001/pcaps.

Aaron (SRE): Initial RCA action items:
- Analyse CF resolver logs + packet captures to find why eu-west POPs saw SERVFAIL/timeouts.
- Add guardrail to auto-rollback geo-weight changes if error rate >5% within 2m.
- Improve canary automation and scaling thresholds.
- Draft customer-facing postmortem and internal blameless postmortem.

Maya (EngOps): Will keep TTL at 30s for 1 hour, then step it up to 300s after 4h of stable metrics. Closing active mitigation unless CF updates otherwise.

John (Support): I'll post a follow-up to customers in 30 minutes with progress and expected timeline.

incident-bot: Incident logged: incident-2026-geo-eu-001. Severity: SEV2 (mitigated, partial customer impact).

Aaron (SRE): Thanks team. If anything regresses, revive this thread.

Maya (EngOps): Note: packet capture paths and a short checklist added to the incident doc for postmortem review.

Raj (CTO): Thanks all. We'll review in the postmortem and decide on next steps with Cloudflare and Route53 relationship. :thumbsup:
